lines: Number, please. No number, no share, and I am afraid a face is not a number.
Oh - the stack. That is different. That is not a share, that is a challenge.
Down the stair, then, and do try to come back up it the proper way.
You have a tally now, which means you are on my board, which means you are my problem.
Column four hundred and twelve. I have had to rule a new one.
Fourth week waiting. My furnace has been cold so long the lining has cracked.
I do not think he is wrong, mind. I have read the board. There is not enough of it.
I just want him to be wrong. It would be so much easier if he were wrong.
He came down himself to tell me. Half an hour on the west tap tonight.
He would not say where he got it. He never does. Somebody is dark for me tonight.
Drawing since Tuesday, and I sit in here anyway, where everyone can see me sitting.
You do not stop coming to this room just because you are warm.
That is how you end up the person everyone in the queue is thinking about.
My grandmother said the fissure was free once. Anybody could sink a flue and take what they liked.
Then the whole east quarter went out in one night, all at once, because everybody took at once.
So they built this room. It is an ugly room and I would not be without it.
The Keeper's up the stack and you cannot get up the stack because the stack is off.
I have tried it eleven times. You do not fall far. You just land somewhere embarrassing.
Down there it is one fire and four hundred arguments and only one beam.
If you get stuck, look at what you are standing on. Rock that glows is going up.
Iron that does not is going down. There is nothing else to it and it takes people a while.
You got up his stack. He has not had one of those in two years.
He will have been perfectly civil about it and then gone straight back to the board. He always does.
